definitions.explanation: Moving or acting slowly and inefficiently, often causing frustration. Implies wasting time or being indecisive.

examples.japanese: もたもたしてると{遅刻|ちこく}するよ。
examples.english: If you keep dilly-dallying, you'll be late.

examples.japanese: もたもたしないで{早|はや}く{準備|じゅんび}して。
examples.english: Stop dawdling and get ready quickly.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のもたもたした{動|うご}きにイライラした。
examples.english: I got irritated by his sluggish movements.

notes:
MIMETIC TYPE:
Onomatopoeia expressing slow, inefficient movement or action.

GRAMMATICAL FORMS:
・もたもたする - to dawdle, be slow (suru-verb)
・もたもた（と）{動|うご}く - to move sluggishly
・もたもたした - sluggish (adjectival)

NUANCE:
Usually carries a negative connotation, implying the person is being annoyingly slow or wasting time. Often used when urging someone to hurry.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・ぐずぐずする - to dawdle, procrastinate
・のろのろ - slowly (more neutral)
・てきぱき - briskly, efficiently (opposite)
